pages.en:
“Hah…………gh.”

Even the simple exertion of walking aggravates it.

My shoulder throbs with every step down the hill. Without noticing, I begin to shorten my stride.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Haa…… guh.”
Even walking hurts my wound.
It hurts every time I take a step, and my strides are getting shorter.

The Emiya residence or the Tohsaka mansion—it makes no difference.

For now, I have to return Tohsaka to friendly ground as quickly as I can.

She shouts at me.

…Right. She still has not recovered herself.

Tohsaka lacks her usual composure.

She has always been passionate. With the brakes broken, perhaps anger is the only thing she can do.

She scolds me.

She’s very emotional, so her anger will be unstoppable if the brakes give way.

“————”

Its vastness steals my breath.

Perhaps we spent too long underground. Perhaps the stars happen to be especially clear tonight.

Whatever the reason, the winter sky is beautiful enough to make me forget the pain in my shoulder.

Even the warmth of Tohsaka's body against my back ceases to trouble me.

For now, I let everything drift away and stare vaguely into the burned-black sky.

”

Anyways, the winter night sky is so beautiful that it makes me forget about my wound.
The warmth of Tohsaka’s body on my back doesn’t bother me either.

pages.jaRuby: 「……別にグチを言うわけじゃないけどね。わたし、いつも一番大事なことばっかりしくじるのよ。二番か三番か、そういうのはさらっと出来るくせに、一番大事なものだけは手こずるんだ」
pages.en: “…I'm not complaining, you understand. It's just that I always fail at the one thing that matters most. I can accomplish the second or third most important thing without effort, but the most important one always gives me trouble.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…I’m not complaining, but I keep on screwing up when it counts the most. I can handle the second and third most important things with ease, but I always have a problem with the single most important one.”

pages.ja:
冬の空は透き通っている。
が、その反面、気温はひどく冷え込んでいた。
俺はともかく、遠坂はコートもないし寒いんじゃないだろうか。
……ちょっと、そのあたりが心配だ。

pages.en:
The winter sky is perfectly clear.

The price of that clarity is a bitter cold.

I may not feel it, but Tohsaka has no coat. She must be freezing.

…That worries me a little.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The winter sky is clear.
But in contrast, the air is really cold.
I don’t care about myself, but isn’t Tohsaka cold without her coat?
…I’m worried about that.

pages.ja:
「アーチャーがあっち側にいったのも、あいつだけの責任じゃないわ。結局、キャスターを野放しにしたのはわたしだもの。
けど、うん……まいったなあ、ついさっきあんなコト言ったのに、いきなり追い詰められちゃった」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Archer going over to their side isn't entirely his fault. In the end, I'm the one who allowed Caster to run free.

“But, yes… this is bad. I said all that only a moment ago, and suddenly I've been driven into a corner.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s not Archer’s fault alone that he went to their side. It’s my fault for letting Caster be.
But yeah… it really gets to me. I was talking to him earlier, but I’m cornered already.”

pages.ja:
はあ、と大きな溜息をつく。
見えないけど、やはりその息も白いのだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
はあ、と大きな溜息をつく。
見えないけど、やはりその息も白いのだろう。
pages.en:
She releases a long sigh.

I cannot see it, but her breath must be white.
pages.mirrorMoon:
She sighs.
I can’t see it, but I bet her breath is white.

pages.ja:
「……ちょっと。ここ、何にってつっこむところだと思うんだけど」
「ああ。で、何に追い詰められたんだ、遠坂」
pages.jaRuby:
「……ちょっと。ここ、何にってつっこむところだと思うんだけど」
「ああ。で、何に追い詰められたんだ、遠坂」
pages.en:
“…Hey. This is where you're supposed to ask, ‘Driven into a corner by what?’”

“Right. What drove you into a corner, Tohsaka?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hey now. I think this is where you make a comment.”
“Oh. So, what were you cornered by, Tohsaka?”

pages.ja:
「うん、後悔はしたくないってコト。
あいつは、わたしはそういう性格じゃないって言ってたけど、今が正念場みたい。士郎があんな事いうから、余計失敗したなー、って落ち込んじゃった」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Well, I said that I don't want to regret anything.

“He said I'm not the sort of person who does, but it seems I've reached the real test. Then you had to say something like that, and it only made me brood even more about how badly I failed.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s about never regretting your own actions.
He said I’m not the type to regret my actions, but it seems now’s the critical moment. I’m even more depressed that I’ve made a mistake.”

pages.ja:
「
」
……なんだ。
言っている事はよく分からないが、アーチャーの言は正しい。
遠坂は後悔をするようなタイプじゃない。
pages.jaRuby:
「
」
……なんだ。
言っている事はよく分からないが、アーチャーの言は正しい。
遠坂は後悔をするようなタイプじゃない。
pages.en:
“————”

…Oh.

I do not entirely follow what she means, but Archer was right.

Tohsaka is not the sort of person who lives with regret.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
…I see.
I don’t understand her too well, but Archer’s right.
Tohsaka isn’t the type to regret her actions.

pages.ja:
「そんなの今だけだろ。癪に障るけど、俺もアーチャーの意見には同感だ。遠坂は、何も反省することなんてない」
「どうしてよ。現にキャスターはやりたい放題で、アーチャーにまで愛想を尽かされた。これ、わたしが方針を間違えたからでしょう」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“You'll only feel that way for now. It irritates me to admit it, but I agree with Archer. You don't have anything to regret, Tohsaka.”

“Why not? Caster is doing whatever she pleases, and even Archer gave up on me. Isn't that because I chose the wrong policy?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“That’s just now, right? It’s irritating, but I agree with Archer. There’s nothing for you to regret.”
“Why? Caster is doing whatever she wants, and even Archer lost faith in me. This is because my policy was a mistake, right?”

pages.ja: 「それは単に失敗しただけだろ。遠坂は間違えてなんかない。間違えていないなら、失敗しても胸を張れると思う」
pages.jaRuby: 「それは単に失敗しただけだろ。遠坂は間違えてなんかない。間違えていないなら、失敗しても胸を張れると思う」
pages.en: “No. It only means you failed. You weren't wrong. If your choice wasn't mistaken, then I think you can hold your head high even in failure.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “It’s just that you were unsuccessful. You haven’t made a mistake. If you haven’t made a mistake, you can be proud of yourself even if you were unsuccessful.”

pages.ja:
その過程。
自らが正しいと信じた道を歩いたのなら、間違いなんてない。
……そういう時、大抵の人間は選んだ道そのものが間違いだったって気が付くワケだけど、こいつは違う。
こいつの選ぶ道は、いつだって胸を張れるものだろうから。
pages.jaRuby:
その過程。
自らが正しいと信じた道を歩いたのなら、間違いなんてない。
……そういう時、大抵の人間は選んだ道そのものが間違いだったって気が付くワケだけど、こいつは違う。
こいつの選ぶ道は、いつだって胸を張れるものだろうから。
pages.en:
——What matters is the path to that failure.

If you walked the course you believed was right, then you made no mistake.

…Of course, most people eventually realize that the path they chose was itself mistaken. But she is different.

Whatever path Tohsaka chooses will always be one she can walk with pride.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The process.
If you walk down the path that you believe is right, you cannot be wrong.
…At a time like this, most people will realize that their path is a wrong one, but she’s different.
Her path should always be one that she can be proud of.

pages.en:
“——Yes. Honestly, you're dazzling to me.

“…I don't regret anything either. I believe that what I've done was right. But that belief is patched together from scraps.”

——I will not regret.

I insist that the path behind me was right only because I cannot bear to let every tragedy that occurred upon it become meaningless.

“But you aren't like that.

“If you regret something, you're the type to pay it back twice over. I hide everything beneath patches, but you smash the whole problem to pieces without changing your expression.

“The accounts balance. You may not get depressed often, but what follows is terrifying. Whoever brought you down will end up several times more miserable than you were.”

“——Ugh. What's that supposed to be, kicking me while I'm down?”

“Yeah. I thought I'd say it while the demon was laid low.

“But it is true, isn't it? You don't intend to leave matters like this.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
Yeah. To be honest, you’ve always shined.
…I won’t regret my actions either. I believe what I’ve done is right, but it’s full of stitches.”
I don’t want to regret anything.
I want to make all the tragedies that happened into meaningful things by believing that my path is right.
“But you’re different.
You’re the type that will regret something, then go back and retaliate. I’m deceiving myself with all the patchwork, but you go and completely destroy it with a straight face.
You’re breaking even. You only get depressed once in a while, but what comes after is scary in your case. I think you will go to the one that got you depressed and get them to be even more depressed.”
“
Ugh. What is that, are you trying to finish me off?”
“Yeah, I thought I’d strike while your guard was down.
Well, isn’t that true? I’m sure you don’t intend to give up now.”

pages.ja:
夜空を見上げながら、こっちも独り言のように言う。
遠坂は答えない。
ただ、なんとなく。
気を取り直したような、微笑がこぼれた気がした。

pages.en:
Still looking up at the night sky, I speak as though continuing a monologue of my own.

Tohsaka does not answer.

But somehow,

I think a smile escapes her, as though she has recovered herself.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I look up at the night sky and say so as if talking to myself.
Tohsaka doesn’t answer.
But I think that…
She smiled, getting herself together.

」

pages.jaRuby:

」

“————”

Then silence.

Perhaps she has said everything she wanted. Tohsaka lapses once more into quiet.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
And silence follows.
Tohsaka must have said everything she wanted to, as she stops talking.

pages.ja:
意味もなく夜空を見上げる。
……すぐにでも家に帰らなくてはいけないのに、どちらも立ち上がれずに背中を合わせている。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
I continue to stare at the night sky for no reason.

…Though we should return home immediately, neither of us can rise. We remain seated back to back.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I aimlessly look up at the night sky.
…We should be going home… But neither one of us can stand up to break the moment, so we just keep our backs to each other.

“——By the way. Why did you save me, Shirou?”

“————”

There is no single answer.

I have any number of reasons.

Explaining each one would feel somehow absurd.

So I say the thing that has to come first.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
Oh yeah. Why did you come help me, Shirou?”
“
”
I can’t explain.
There are many reasons.
I think it’d be stupid to explain each one.
So I say something I have to tell her.

じゃら、と音をたててペンダントを見せる。
pages.jaRuby:

“You recognize this pendant, don't you?”

It jingles as I hold it up.

“You remember this pendant, right?”
I show her the pendant.

」

pages.jaRuby:

”

…I thought so. I bet she intended to keep this a secret, but she made a mistake again.

pages.en:
“Wait… Why do you have that?”

“I found it in your room. Oh… You'll be surprised when you go home, but sorry. I knocked over your dressing table.”

“Here,” I add, passing the pendant back to her over my shoulder.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hey… where did you get that?”
“I found it in your room. Oh… You might get surprised when you get home, but I’m sorry. I tipped over your dresser.”
I return her the pendant behind my back.

“…Hmph. And what exactly is that supposed to mean to you?”

“Well. There's an identical pendant at my house.

“When Lancer nearly killed me at school, I found it lying beside me when I came to. I picked it up, and I've kept it ever since.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Heh. So what about it?”
“Well, I have the exact same pendant at my house.
I picked it up when I found it after being killed by Lancer.”

と

I allude as harmlessly as possible to what happened that night.

And then—

“——There is another one… exactly like it?”

Tohsaka draws a sharp breath, as though she has seen something she was never meant to see.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I casually hint about that night.
Then
“
There’s an identical one…?”
Tohsaka gasps as if she’s heard something she shouldn’t have.

pages.en:
“Huh? Did I say something strange?”

“Ah… No, nothing. …More importantly, why would that make you save me? It's only a pendant. It doesn't matter.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Huh? Did I say something strange?”
“Uh… no, it’s nothing. But why would that be a reason to come help me? That pendant means nothing, right?”

pages.ja:

白状すると、ずっと前から遠坂凛ってやつに憧れてた。
で、困ったコトにいざ話してみたら余計好きになっちまった。だから死んでほしくなくて、気が付けば、何も考えずに飛び降りていただけだ」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“You're right. …Honestly, that's only a reason I added afterward.

“The truth is, I've admired Rin Tohsaka for a long time.

“And then, inconveniently enough, I liked you even more once we actually spoke. I didn't want you to die. Before I knew it, I had jumped without thinking about anything at all.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Right. …It’s just a reason I made up afterwards.
To confess, I’ve been admiring Tohsaka Rin for a long time.
And this is a problem, but I got to like you even more after I talked to you. So I didn’t want you to die, and I jumped down even before I realized it.”

“Hmph. Who could misunderstand that? I really do like you, Tohsaka.”

I answer at once, too stubborn to retreat.

It is neither a lie nor anything resembling one. There is nothing to misunderstand.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I won’t create misunderstandings. I really do like you.”
I obstinately reply at once.
It’s not a lie, so there’s no misunderstanding to be made.

pages.ja: 「ば、ばかっ……！ そんなんだから自殺同然で飛び込んでくるのよ、この大馬鹿っ！」

pages.mirrorMoon: “Y-You idiot…! That’s why you jumped in suicidally, you big idiot!”

pages.en:
Tohsaka calls me an idiot over and over.

I am being abused mercilessly, yet somehow I do not mind in the least.

The night sky is beautiful. My heart is at peace.

More than anything, I am truly glad that Tohsaka has become herself again.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka keeps calling me an idiot.
She’s criticizing mercilessly, but I strangely don’t feel bad.
The night sky is beautiful, and I feel calm.
And I’m just really happy that Tohsaka’s back to normal.

pages.ja: 「よし。士郎の言うとおり、そろそろ家に帰りましょうか」
pages.jaRuby: 「よし。士郎の言うとおり、そろそろ家に帰りましょうか」
pages.en: “All right. Just as you said, Shirou, we should be getting home.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “All right. Let’s go home like you said.”

pages.ja:
「ほら、手を出して。その傷だと立つのも辛いでしょ」
差し出された手を右手で握る。
よっ、なんて元気のいい声をだして、遠坂は俺をひっぱりあげた。

pages.en:
“Here, give me your hand. Standing must be difficult with that wound.”

I take her offered hand in my right.

With a brisk “Up you go,” Tohsaka pulls me to my feet.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Here, give me your hand. It should be hard for you to stand up with that wound of yours.”
I grab her hand with my right.
Tohsaka pulls me up.

pages.ja: 「これで貸し借りはなしね。今日の事はお互いノーカウントって事にしましょ」
pages.jaRuby: 「これで貸し借りはなしね。今日の事はお互いノーカウントって事にしましょ」
pages.en: “That clears the debt between us. Let's agree that nothing either of us did today counts.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Then we don’t owe each other anything now. Let’s not count today’s incident.”

あのペンダントが遠坂にとってどんな物だったのか、俺は知らない。

それを嫌って遠坂は相殺すると言った。

pages.en:
“————”

Yes. That helps.

I do not know what that pendant meant to Tohsaka.

If I learned, I might feel that I owed her an even greater debt.

To prevent that, she declared our accounts even.

And so Tohsaka need not feel indebted because I saved her either.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“
”
That would really help me out.
I don’t know what the pendant meant to Tohsaka.
I bet I would have felt more guilty towards Tohsaka if I found out.
Tohsaka didn’t want that and said the incidents offset one another.
So Tohsaka shouldn’t feel bad about getting helped earlier.

pages.ja:
そうして、外人墓地を後にする。
その道中、ぽつりと、
「……助けてくれてありがとう士郎。その、すっごく助かったわ」
照れくさそうに、遠坂は付け足していた。

pages.en:
——We leave the foreign cemetery.

On the way, quietly—

“…Thank you for saving me, Shirou. It… really did mean a lot.”

Tohsaka adds the words with visible embarrassment.
pages.mirrorMoon:
And we leave the foreigners’ cemetery.
And on the way…
“…Thanks for helping me, Shirou. Um, it really did help me out.”
Tohsaka adds with embarrassment.

pages.ja:
坂道を下っていく。
安心できるホームグラウンドに帰ろう、という時。
遠坂は当然のように、自分の家ではなく、衛宮邸を目指していた。
pages.jaRuby:
坂道を下っていく。
安心できるホームグラウンドに帰ろう、という時。
遠坂は当然のように、自分の家ではなく、[ruby text=おれのいえ char=3]衛宮邸を目指していた。
pages.en:
We descend the hill.

As we set out for the safety of familiar ground, Tohsaka naturally heads not toward her own mansion,

but toward *my home*, the Emiya residence.
pages.mirrorMoon:
We walk down the hill.
When we’re going back to our home ground where it’s safe…
Tohsaka heads for my house and not her house, as if it’s natural to do so.
